newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK post-handover stock picks carry China theme - poll.
newsitem.headline: HK post-handover stock picks carry China theme - poll.

text.p: Hong Kong stock analysts are placing their bets on China-focused shares in the year following the territory's return to China, according to a survey conducted by Reuters this week.

Asked for their top-10 picks in the post-handover period, nine Hong Kong-based analysts produced portfolios with strong China themes, featuring blue chip Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and red chip China Resources Enterprise Ltd.
"The Hong Kong market right now is more influenced by the Chinese market and the Chinese economy than anything else," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
Hong Kong returns to China at midnight of June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule. In the run up to the transition, the stock market has been heavily focused on China-related plays.
Appearing in seven of the nine suggested portfolios was Hong Kong property developer Cheung Kong.

"It is an anchor constituent of the Hang Seng Index with friendly China relations, attractive valuations and diversification through Hutchison Whampoa Ltd into container terminals, property and telecoms," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Next came China Resources, appearing in six of the nine portfolios. Rossiter also chose the stock along with red chip Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd.
"You'll need some exposure to China and these two have definitely got it. Quality guanxi (connections) are going to differentiate the leaders from those that languish," he said.
New World Development Co Ltd, COSCO Pacific Ltd and Swire Pacific Ltd all came next, with four out of nine analysts picking the stocks.
New World has been touted as a China play due to its large China land bank, and analysts said profit contributions from its mainland businesses were set to grow in coming years.
"New World Development and Cheung Kong are obvious core holdings. Clearly they have advantages getting into China," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"They have gotten in early and they understand the system. They have done enough deals in China and can operate in the post 1997 environment effectively," he said.
Fernow also had red chips China Resources and COSCO Pacific Ltd in his top-10 picks.

"The reason behind that is they have very strong parents which will support these companies in the immediate post-handover period so as to elevate the stature and the profile of these companies," he said.
"There you can anticipate more asset injections because the companies have already done some and another round of expansion is widely anticipated."
Analysts said they had picked Swire Pacific, a market laggard, for its potential for growth in China.

The company's colonial ties as an old British "hong", or trading house, have served as a drag on its shares this year but the company said recently it would like to develop its China business more rapidly in coming years.
"Sooner or later it should have a strong China connection," said DBS Securities director of research Percy Au-young.
The following are the top-10 picks of the nine brokerage firms polled:

BNP PRIMEEAST SECURITIES: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, CITIC Pacific Ltd, Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd, Cheung Kong, Swire Pacific, Ka Wah Bank Ltd, Founder (Hong Kong) Ltd, China Resources Beijing Land Ltd, China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd, China Light & Power Co Ltd.

DBS SECURITIES: Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd, Hang Seng Bank Ltd, Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd, Hsin Chong Construction Group Ltd, Hysan Development Co Ltd, New World Infrastructure Ltd, Semi-Tech (Global) Co Ltd, Shougang Concord Grand (Group) Ltd, Swire Pacific, Varitronix International Ltd.

DELTA ASIA SECURITIES: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd HK, Cheung Kong, New World Development, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd , Swire Pacific, Amoy Properties Ltd, Hysan Development, Great Eagle Holdings Ltd, IDT International Ltd, Min Xin Holdings Ltd.

NIKKO SECURITIES: China Resources, Shanghai Industrial, Hang Seng Bank, FPB Bank Holding Co Ltd, New World Development, Cheung Kong, Aeon Credit Service (Asia) Co Ltd, GZI Transport Ltd, Asia Satellite Telecommunications Holdings Ltd, Lung Kee (Bermuda) Holdings Ltd.
